steps.name: Warm-up recognition pass
steps.script: 3–4 min. Show the full 28-letter set in fully randomized order (not grouped by shape-family). Student names each letter and produces its sound. No scoring pressure communicated — this is a warm-up — but quietly note any hesitation/error on the scoring sheet.

audio.cue: ا: open, unobstructed sound from the empty space of the mouth/chest cavity (al-jawf) — no glottal catch added
ب: both lips close fully, then release — like English b but with complete lip contact
ت: tongue-tip taps the ridge behind the upper front teeth — light, no heaviness
ث: tongue-tip BETWEEN the teeth, unvoiced 'th' as in think — never plain t, never s
ج: middle of the tongue rises to the roof of the mouth — a soft 'j' affricate, not a hard g
ح: strong, unvoiced, breathy friction from the MIDDLE of the throat — like fogging a mirror; heavier than ه, distinct from خ
خ: back of the tongue against the soft palate, UPPER throat — a rough 'kh' friction
د: tongue-tip taps the upper gum ridge — a plain, light 'd', never voiced toward ذ
ذ: tongue-tip BETWEEN the teeth, voiced 'th' as in this — never collapse to a plain 'z'
ر: tongue-tip curls slightly and taps the gum ridge ONCE — a light single flap, never a static English/Uzbek 'r'
ز: tongue-tip near the lower teeth, a plain voiced hiss — 'z', keep distinct from ذ
س: tongue-tip near the lower teeth, a thin unvoiced hiss — plain 's'
ش: middle of the tongue against the roof of the mouth — 'sh', keep crisp, don't blur with س
ص: heavy twin of س — back of tongue raised, fuller mouth cavity, a thick emphatic hiss
ض: side of the tongue releases against the upper molars — a lateral release unique to this letter; the hardest letter in the alphabet, go slow
ط: heavy twin of ت — tongue-tip taps the gum ridge but with a held, forceful, full-mouth-echo release
ظ: heavy twin of ذ — tongue-tip between the teeth, voiced, with the full emphatic darkness added
ع: a muscular squeeze/constriction in the MIDDLE of the throat, voiced — a real squeeze, not just a glottal stop (that's ء)
غ: upper throat, same zone as خ but voiced — a uvular fricative, close to a French uvular 'r', stays a friction not a stop
ف: inner edge of the lower lip against the tips of the upper front teeth — plain 'f'
ق: back of the tongue against the soft palate — a deep uvular, 'cough-like' stop, heavier and further back than ك
ك: back of the tongue against the soft palate, but shallower and lighter than ق — a plain 'k'
ل: tip/sides of the tongue against the gum ridge — a clear, light 'l'
م: both lips closed, sound resonates through the nose — nasal 'm'
ن: tongue-tip against the gum ridge, released with nasal resonance — a two-part sound, oral release plus nasal buzz
ه: a soft, breathy 'h' from an open throat — much lighter and shallower than ح, don't darken it
و: lips rounded, a consonant 'w' (its long-vowel role comes later — ignore that for now)
ي: middle of tongue near the roof of the mouth, a consonant 'y' (its long-vowel role comes later — ignore that for now)

steps.name: Makhraj spot-check
steps.script: 8–10 min. Select 10 of the 14 high-risk letters below at random each sitting (so no two checkpoints are identical). For each: student produces the sound AND states in plain English where it's articulated (e.g. "mid-throat," "tip of tongue between the teeth," "the two lips"). Tests self-aware correctness, not just rote muscle memory.

audio.cue: ح: strong, unvoiced, breathy friction from the MIDDLE of the throat — like fogging a mirror; heavier than ه, distinct from خ
خ: back of the tongue against the soft palate, UPPER throat — a rough 'kh' friction
ه: a soft, breathy 'h' from an open throat — much lighter and shallower than ح, don't darken it
ع: a muscular squeeze/constriction in the MIDDLE of the throat, voiced — a real squeeze, not just a glottal stop (that's ء)
ء: a plain glottal stop — the catch before an English word starting with a vowel; deep in the throat but no muscular squeeze (that squeeze is ع)
ص: heavy twin of س — back of tongue raised, fuller mouth cavity, a thick emphatic hiss
ض: side of the tongue releases against the upper molars — a lateral release unique to this letter; the hardest letter in the alphabet, go slow
ط: heavy twin of ت — tongue-tip taps the gum ridge but with a held, forceful, full-mouth-echo release
ظ: heavy twin of ذ — tongue-tip between the teeth, voiced, with the full emphatic darkness added
ذ: tongue-tip BETWEEN the teeth, voiced 'th' as in this — never collapse to a plain 'z'
ز: tongue-tip near the lower teeth, a plain voiced hiss — 'z', keep distinct from ذ
ق: back of the tongue against the soft palate — a deep uvular, 'cough-like' stop, heavier and further back than ك
ك: back of the tongue against the soft palate, but shallower and lighter than ق — a plain 'k'
ر: tongue-tip curls slightly and taps the gum ridge ONCE — a light single flap, never a static English/Uzbek 'r'

steps.name: Positional reading
steps.script: 5–7 min. Present 6 unvoweled 2–3 letter clusters built to include at least 2 non-connector letters (listed below) and at least 2 letters shown in medial form. Student reads each aloud, correctly identifying every component letter regardless of shape.

audio.cue: ا: non-connector — never joins to the letter that follows it, though it still joins to the letter before it
د: non-connector — tongue-tip taps the upper gum ridge; never joins to the letter that follows it
ذ: non-connector — tongue-tip between the teeth, voiced; never joins to the letter that follows it
ر: non-connector — light single tongue-tap; never joins to the letter that follows it
ز: non-connector — plain voiced hiss; never joins to the letter that follows it
و: non-connector — lips rounded consonant 'w'; never joins to the letter that follows it

steps.name: Vowel grid spot-check
steps.script: 8–10 min. Sample 20 cells at random from the full 84-cell letter × harakat grid — not a fixed pre-known set, genuinely randomized each sitting so the student cannot pre-memorize a specific sequence. Student reads each cell aloud.

steps.name: Syllable transfer test
steps.script: 5–7 min. Present 5–6 abstract 2–3 syllable combinations the student has NOT seen in any prior lesson or homework sheet (freshly built from the same letter/vowel inventory). Student decodes each — the one genuinely unseen-material test in the checkpoint. Score hesitation/self-correction leniently: a student who stumbles but self-corrects without teacher intervention should not be penalized as harshly as one who cannot produce the sound at all.

steps.name: Wrap-up
steps.script: 2–3 min. Complete the scoring sheet with the student present, state the pass/revise result plainly, and — if extra practice is needed — name the specific lesson(s) to revisit (see the weak-spot map below) rather than "do Phase 1 again."

steps.name: Record results
steps.script: Print this page; per rubric row mark pass / revise, note the mapped revision lessons, date and sign.

rubric.criterion: Lahn Jali (major) errors — 28-letter warm-up + makhraj spot-check
rubric.pass: Zero. Any unrecognizable letter or wrong-phoneme production is a hard-fail item regardless of how well the rest of the session goes.

rubric.criterion: Lahn Khafi (minor) flags — whole session total
rubric.pass: ≤3 total → pass, with a homework flag naming the specific letters/qualities to keep practicing at home (no retest required).

rubric.criterion: Single-letter Jali errors — breadth across distinct letters
rubric.pass: Must not occur on more than 2 distinct letters — otherwise the checkpoint does not pass.

rubric.criterion: Jali errors — vowel-grid spot-check (step 4, 20 sampled cells)
rubric.pass: Fewer than 2. Two or more Jali errors in this step fails the checkpoint.
Decode at least 3 of the 5–6 items — failing to decode 3 or more fails the checkpoint. Self-corrected hesitation is scored leniently, not penalized like an examiner-corrected miss.
4 or more total Khafi flags fails the checkpoint even if every Jali criterion above is met.

revisionMap.weakSpot: ص / ض / ط / ظ tafkheem quality (heaviness under- or mis-applied)
ع substituted with ء, or غ/خ/ق confusion
ذ / ز / ض "D→Z" collapse pattern (any pair merging)
ق flattened toward ك (or vice versa)
Non-connector rule not applied (ا د ذ ر ز و)
General cluster-reading hesitation/pace, no specific letter culprit
Fatha timing/quality (lengthened into madd, or heavy-letter darkening missing)
Syllable-transfer decoding failures with no single letter/vowel culprit (fluency issue, not accuracy)
Sukūn mis-read — a vowel added after the closed letter, or the sukūn lengthened
Hamza dropped, or its seat (أ إ ؤ ئ) sounded as a waaw/yaa
Qalqalah missing on ق ط ب ج د with sukūn, or wrongly applied to ظ
Heaviness audible on the consonant but absent from the vowel beside it
A hard letter correct alone but degrading when a second hard letter follows in the same word
Word reading accurate only when the target letter is announced in advance
